The two members are standard vectors, and the member-initializer list already selects each vector's copy constructor, which does exactly one allocation plus a bulk element copy with no temporaries or reallocation. I kept that minimal form (rather than default-constructing and then assigning in the body, which adds a capacity check and redundant pointer setup), so the compiler emits the tightest possible two-vector copy.

```cpp
FieldBase::FieldBase(const FieldBase &field)
    : values(field.values)
    , stringIndexes(field.stringIndexes)
{
}
```
